title: Introducing Aglide SMS
summary: Legacy banking portals, EHRs, and insurance platforms often only support SMS 2FA. That makes shared accounts a nightmare, offboarding unreliable, and full lifecycle automation impossible. Aglide SMS gives IT teams managed phone numbers that handle all of it automatically.
body_text: Aglide's goal is to connect every non-SAML and non-SCIM application to your identity provider - letting admins automate any lifecycle task, and giving end-users a seamless SSO login experience. To do that, we need to be able to handle every kind of credential an application might could use. Aglide already managed email addresses for magic links and email OTP, and TOTP secrets for authenticator-based 2FA. Today we're adding the final piece, with the launch of Aglide SMS, Aglide can now automate phone number based authentication systems. The Problem Legacy applications, particularly in banking, healthcare, and insurance, haven't caught up with modern authentication standards. Many still only support SMS as a second factor. No TOTP option, no magic link. If you want to log in, you need a phone number.That creates three problems. SMS 2FA is a nightmare for shared accounts When a shared account is gated by SMS, every login depends on tracking down whoever owns the number - typically over Slack, a shared inbox, or a phone sitting on someone's desk. More often than not, it's tied to someone's personal number. When that person leaves, so does the ability to log in. SMS 2FA is insecure Phone numbers can be SIM swapped. A shared account number - often undocumented, unmonitored, and attached to no formal owner - is an easy target. SMS 2FA was never strong; on shared accounts, it's particularly weak. SMS 2FA blocks automation When Aglide signs into an application to complete a SCIM lifecycle task (e.g., provisioning, deprovisioning, etc.), it needs to authenticate through whatever 2FA method the app requires. Without SMS support, any SMS-only app would pause the workflow and prompt a user to input the code manually. Aglide SMS Admins can now provision Aglide-managed phone numbers and assign them to both individual user accounts and shared accounts. Seamless SSO login: When a user signs in to an individual or shared application that uses an Aglide SMS number via Aglide SSO, all they need to do is complete their SSO login, Aglide will handle automatically receive the SMS code and complete authentication automatically. Complete lifecycle automation: Provisioning, deprovisioning, and access reviews run end-to-end across SMS-gated applications without exception handling. Full 2FA coverage: Combined with Aglide Managed Emails and TOTP Secrets, Aglide now handles every major automated 2FA method. For anything else, Aglide surfaces the UI to the user directly. Security As with everything in Aglide, we took an immense amount of care to ensure this is implemented as securely as possible. Aglide SMS is powered by Twilio, but Twilio has no visibility into which phone number belongs to which user. When Twilio forwards a message to Aglide, the contents are immediately encrypted with the recipient user's local public key using Aglide's zero-trust model. This means: Aglide can't read SMS your messages. Messages can only be decrypted by the user on their own device, using their local key. Users cannot read each other's messages. Each number's messages are encrypted to a single user's key, that only that user has. SIM swap risk is eliminated. Aglide-managed numbers are not tied to a physical SIM or carrier account in the traditional sense. There is no social engineering vector to hijack them. What This Means in Practice For IT teams managing access across a broad application estate, Aglide SMS removes the last manual step in automated provisioning. Applications that previously required a human in the loop for SMS 2FA - whether for day-to-day authentication or IdP lifecycle tasks - can now be fully automated. For security and compliance teams, it replaces an uncontrolled pattern (shared numbers, personal phones, Slack-distributed codes) with one that is managed, attributable, and auditable by default. Aglide now covers the full range of 2FA methods across your application estate: Method Aglide support SMS Aglide-managed numbers, fully automated Email OTP / magic link Aglide-managed addresses, fully automated TOTP Aglide-managed secrets, fully automated Other methods UI surfaced directly to the user Aglide SMS was developed after a key design partner - a $20Bn financial services company - told us they wanted to connect their 70 treasury banking portals, including JP Morgan and Wells Fargo, to Okta to enable SSO and automate lifecycle management. SMS 2FA was the blocker. We'd like to thank them for their feedback and partnership in building this. Aglide SMS is available now. Contact your account team or reach out at hello@aglide.com to get started.

title: ImmuneOnco Announced Preliminary Safety & Efficacy Data from the Clinical Trial Studying IMM2510/AXN-2510, a PD-L1xVEGF Bispecific Antibody, in Combination with Chemotherapy in Front-line NSCLC in China
summary: Partial responses observed in 80% of squamous NSCLC front-line patients and in 46% of non-squamous NSCLC front-line patients Safety profile supports further clinical development, with no dose-limiting toxicities observed in patients with front-line NSCLC ImmuneOnco expects to present updated safety
body_text: PDF Version Partial responses observed in 80% of squamous NSCLC front-line patients and in 46% of non-squamous NSCLC front-line patients Safety profile supports further clinical development, with no dose-limiting toxicities observed in patients with front-line NSCLC ImmuneOnco expects to present updated safety and efficacy data at a future medical conference DALLAS and SHANGHAI, July 31, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Instil Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: TIL, “Instil”) noted that ImmuneOnco Biopharmaceuticals (Shanghai) Inc. (HKEX Code: 1541.HK) (“ImmuneOnco”), today announced preliminary safety and efficacy data from the Phase 2 open-label, multicenter study of IMM2510/AXN-2510 (‘2510) in combination with chemotherapy for front-line patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) conducted in China by ImmuneOnco. As of July 1, 2025, 33 patients were dosed at 10 mg/kg, with 21 patients having at least one tumor assessment (efficacy evaluable). Partial responses were observed in 62% of efficacy evaluable patients, comprising partial responses in 80% (8/10) of patients with squamous NSCLC and 46% (5/11) of patients with non-squamous NSCLC. The majority of efficacy evaluable patients had only one tumor assessment at data cut-off. ImmuneOnco expects to present safety and efficacy data in the ‘2510 chemotherapy combination trial in front-line NSCLC at a future medical conference. The ‘2510 safety profile supports further clinical development, with no dose-limiting toxicities observed in the 33 safety evaluable patients. In these patients, there were no treatment-related adverse events (TRAE) leading to dose reduction or death, and only one TRAE leading to drug discontinuation. The most common Grade 3+ TRAEs were hematologic, with uncommon clinical sequelae. Adverse events typically associated with VEGF inhibition (e.g., hypertension, proteinuria, hemoptysis) and immune-related adverse events were uncommon and generally low-grade, and infusion-related reactions were nearly all low-grade. “‘2510 has demonstrated early but compelling activity in front-line NSCLC patients,” said Professor Caicun Zhou, M.D., Ph.D., director of the Department of Oncology at Shanghai East Hospital, Tongji University, and lead investigator on the study of ‘2510 in 1L NSCLC. “The PD-(L)1xVEGF bispecific class has the potential to become the new standard of care for front-line NSCLC, and I look forward to the generation of additional data with ‘2510 in this setting.” Dr. Tian Wenzhi, CEO of ImmuneOnco, said “We are delighted to witness the progress of ‘2510 in front-line non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This data paves the way for its advancement into Phase 3 clinical studies and provides valuable insights to support further research across multiple indications.” “We are pleased with the preliminary clinical results of the combination of ‘2510 with chemotherapy in patients with front-line NSCLC, which suggest the potential for best-in-class efficacy in the promising PD-(L)1xVEGF bispecific antibody class,” said Bronson Crouch, CEO of Instil. “We look forward to further public updates from ImmuneOnco on these data, as well as the initiation of our previously announced US phase 1 clinical trial before the end of this year.” About IMM2510/AXN-2510 IMM2510/AXN-2510 is a PD-L1xVEGF bispecific antibody in development for the treatment of multiple solid tumors. IMM2510/AXN-2510 is differentiated from other PD-(L)1xVEGF bispecific antibodies by its VEGF trap, which binds multiple VEGF receptor ligands beyond VEGF-A, a bispecific structure which leverages PD-L1 as an anchor in the tumor microenvironment (TME), and enhanced antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) to direct killing of PD-L1-positive tumor cells. About ImmuneOnco ImmuneOnco is a clinical-stage biotech company focused on discovery and development of biologics to treat cancers, autoimmune diseases and metabolic diseases. With 10+ assets all originated in-house and the most advanced asset in phase III right now, ImmuneOnco is pursuing innovative therapies to improve patients’ health. For more information visit www.immuneonco.com . About Instil Bio Instil Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a pipeline of novel therapies. Instil's lead asset, AXN-2510, is a novel and differentiated PD-L1xVEGF bispecific antibody in development for the treatment of multiple solid tumors. For more information, visit www.instilbio.com . title: Acceleration Sensing for Active Damping
body_text: The chassis acceleration sensor from CTS Corporation is a flexible, single axis accelerometer device that enables critical active suspension and damping functionalities for all manner of automotive vehicles. Measuring acceleration motion, the chassis acceleration sensor transmits crucial data to the vehicle’s electronic control unit (ECU), in turn enabling real-time damping forces to counteract the detrimental effects for instance shock impacts and body roll. These active damping responses lead to a safer and more comfortable driving experience, significantly improving the driver’s control of the vehicle. Suspension Systems in Modern Vehicles Vehicles of all kinds employ a multitude of springs, linkages, arms and dampers to absorb bumps and shocks, maintain proper tire contact with the road surface and improve the overall vehicle handling by mitigating the shifting weight distribution when turning. Together, these components constitute the vehicle’s suspension system. Such systems have long since become an absolute necessity in any vehicle type, be it commercial, passenger-oriented or otherwise. A well-functioning suspension system is a critical automotive feature that not only ensures a certain level of ride comfort to which drivers and passengers have been accustomed, but also improves vehicle control, making driving safer in general. In older vehicle models, suspension systems were purely passive, meaning that they would simply react to the forces they were exposed to, providing rudimental alleviation. In modern vehicles, however, suspension systems are becoming much more advanced. A range of electronics, sensors and actuators are employed to adjust suspension system behavior in real-time in response to changing driving conditions. The ability to detect dynamic motion and apply appropriate counter-forces greatly increases the driver’s control of the vehicle and makes for a safer, smoother and more pleasant driving experience. See Product Page Advantages of Active Suspension The advantages of active vehicle suspension are numerous and easy to recognize. When a vehicle is forced to make a sudden and sharp turn, its body weight will shift outwards (known as ‘body roll’), causing it to lean into the corner and consequently reduce the tires’ contact with the surface. A passive suspension system will not be able to quickly compensate for this dynamic shift in motion, leading to diminished control of the vehicle for the driver and potentially to unsafe situations. With an active suspension system, however, acceleration sensors will immediately detect the lateral body roll of the vehicle and transmit this information to its electronic control unit (ECU). Using this information, the ECU will instantly signal the wheel actuators to stiffen the outer suspension and lowering the inner side in order to mitigate the body roll and stabilize the vehicle. This feature leads to more flat cornering in general with improved road grip and ride comfort. An active suspension system will enable such active damping forces for the instant adjustment to dynamic vehicle motions. Sharp turns, sudden acceleration and deceleration as well as bumps and potholes in the road all become easier and safer to negotiate for an overall improved and more secure driving experience. The CTS Chassis Acceleration Sensor To enable active suspension systems of modern vehicles, CTS Corporation has developed the chassis acceleration sensor . Mounted on the vehicle’s chassis or body, this accelerometer technology will measure the dynamic motion of the vehicle using a MEMS chip and transmit the information by means of a PSI5 protocol to the ECU, enabling appropriate adjustment of the active damping forces in the suspension system. The chassis acceleration sensor can provide single and, by implementing several units, multi-axis sensing for measuring the full range of dynamic vehicle motion. It has a high bandwidth for highly accurate acceleration readings and can be configured to two different active sensing ranges to meet specific system requirements. In terms of mechanical design, the chassis acceleration sensor has been built with both simplicity and robustness in mind. It is very flexible in terms of mounting position and can easily be adapted to fit a wide range of applications and system architectures. The robust design also allows full EMC compliance, a wide operating temperature range and high resilience to mud, gravel, water and ice exposure. Together with CTS’ proven Ride Height Sensors (RHS) , our suite provides OEMs and Tier 1s with a modular, scalable foundation for advanced vehicle suspension and body dynamics. From electric vehicles to high-performance platforms, our portfolio empowers manufacturers to deliver safer, smoother and more personalized driving experiences. title: Data Share Is GA 🚀 Share Dashboards, Reports, and Datasets
summary: We’re excited to announce that Data Share is officially generally available — and it’s more powerful than ever.
body_text: We’re excited to announce that Data Share is officially generally available — and it’s more powerful than ever. Export dashboards, reports, or raw data directly with your users through Email or to their own S3 Bucket — all without engineering effort. Simplifying data distribution — without custom builds For many SaaS platforms, securely sharing data externally has been a persistent challenge. At Explo, our mission has always been to make it easy for teams to deliver data to their customers. With this latest release, we’re unlocking even more flexible, secure ways to do just that. Each customer expects different data to come in a different form, whether it's in visual dashboards, customer reports, or raw data. Product teams often resort to building and maintaining custom APIs, one-off data pipelines, or spinning up separate reporting portals — all of which require continuous engineering support. Data Share eliminates these bottlenecks. With just a few clicks inside Explo, you can now share: Dashboards and reports: embed screenshots of dashboards and reports into emails. Datasets: Share raw data in CSVs and excel files powered by global datasets on any scheduled cadence. Compared to our existing email sequences, Data Share provides more granular scheduling and recipient lists, so each customer can receive their data on their own cadence. And now, with flexible delivery options — Email and direct to S3 — you can meet your customers and partners where they are, whether that means sharing direct links via email or delivering data to their cloud storage. Over the next couple of weeks, we’ll be launching additional delivery methods from SFTP, to external APIs, slack, and direct data warehouse sync. Built-in security and governance Data Share is built with robust permissioning and governance at its core. You stay in full control: Define who has access to each dashboard or dataset Monitor usage directly within Explo This allows teams to confidently meet compliance requirements while still delivering a flexible, self-service experience to stakeholders. Real-world use cases We’re already seeing customers adopt Data Share for a range of critical workflows: Exporting large datasets: Push any amount of data directly to your customers’ S3 bucket Partner collaboration: Seamlessly exchange joint data sets or performance dashboards with external partners. Internal reporting: Email curated views with sales, finance, and leadership teams — without building redundant internal reporting tools. Fully self-service for product and data teams With Data Share, product and data teams stay empowered. There’s no need for ongoing developer support, API development, or complex integrations. Once configured, Data Share handles the delivery — whether that’s sending automated emails or delivering files directly to S3 buckets. 👉 Ready to simplify your external data sharing workflows? Learn more about Data Share here . ‍ Frequently Asked Questions How do I get started with Data Share? Data Share is available in the Explo App and available to all Pro tier and Enterprise Tier customers. For more detailed costs, reach out to your account manger. What can I share with Explo’s Data Share? Data Share includes the ability to create Scheduled Shares of Dashboards and Global Datasets. Shares are able to be sent to emails or to Amazon S3 buckets with more destinations to come. How does my customer set up their S3 bucket to receive data from Explo? End users will need to provide the appropriate permissions and Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for their S3 Bucket to be able to receive Shares.

title: Celularity Hails New Florida Law Opening Patient Access to Stem Cell Therapies
body_text: Celularity Hails New Florida Law Opening Patient Access to Stem Cell Therapies By Celularity Inc. in Press Releases New law goes into effect on July 1st authorizing Florida physicians to provide stem cell therapies to their patients for orthopedics, wound care, and pain management FLORHAM PARK, N.J., July 01, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Celularity Inc. (Nasdaq: CELU) (“Celularity” or the “Company”), a regenerative and cellular medicine company, today hailed a new Florida law taking effect today that opens the door to physicians’ use of investigational stem cell therapies in the state in orthopedics, wound care, and pain management. “Today, a groundbreaking new law takes effect in Florida authorizing physicians to provide stem cell therapies to their patients subject to strict requirements ensuring patient safety and ethical standards,” said Robert J. Hariri, M.D., Ph.D., Celularity CEO and Chairman. “Celularity is fully prepared to supply the ethically sourced stem cells which enable these treatments, and we look forward to working with Florida physicians to make these innovative therapies available to patients.” The new law authorizes Florida physicians to provide stem cell therapies that have not yet been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, and imposes strict limits on the permissible sources of the stem cells used, which must be manufactured, stored and retrieved in facilities that are FDA registered and certified or accredited by approved organizations. Approved facilities must comply with Good Manufacturing Practices, which are FDA-established standards that mandate strict controls on facilities, processes, and quality control. Additionally, physicians must obtain patient informed consent prior to administering treatments authorized under the new law. “We applaud Florida’s intention to advance medical treatments and improve patient outcomes with this balanced approach to fostering medical innovation while upholding ethical standards,” said Dr. Hariri. “Celularity is the long-standing leader in the field of ethically sourced stem cell therapies with extensive knowledge and real world data obtained from multiple clinical trials, including wound care and other therapeutic targets authorized under the new Florida law.” In 2001, Celularity’s predecessor organization, Anthrogenesis Corporation (later Celgene Cellular Therapeutics) announced a groundbreaking discovery of a method to recover a then-novel kind of stem cell from the postpartum human placenta. President George W. Bush acknowledged this transformational discovery around ethically sourced stem cells in his landmark August 2001 speech on stem cell research. “We believe Florida’s physician-focused approach is a model for other states, insofar as physicians are ideally positioned to assess which therapeutic approach is in a patient’s best interest, including investigational stem cell therapies,” said Dr. Hariri, noting the Florida Medical Association’s statement that it “was extensively involved in the crafting of this legislation and sought to ensure that a proper balance was struck between protecting the public from bogus therapies and preventing physician overregulation.” Celularity operates a purpose-built cell therapy manufacturing and storage/retrieval facility with hundreds of units of placenta-derived stem cells in inventory for use in investigational therapies including those authorized under the new Florida law. Celularity’s facility is FDA registered and certified/accredited as required by the new Florida law. “Celularity is positioned right now to supply the stem cells necessary to fulfill the objectives of the new Florida law and we look forward to working with Florida physicians to ensure their patients have access to stem cell therapies,” said Dr. Hariri. About Celularity Celularity Inc. (Nasdaq: CELU) is a regenerative and cellular medicine company developing and commercializing advanced biomaterial products and allogeneic, cryopreserved, placental-derived cell therapies, all derived from the postpartum placenta. Celularity believes that by harnessing the placenta’s unique biology and ready availability, it can develop therapeutic solutions that address significant unmet global needs for effective, accessible, and affordable therapies. For more information about Celularity and its cutting-edge regenerative medicine solutions, please visit www.celularity.com. title: Supporting Students: How Vanderbilt’s Michelle Parsons Leverages Flo Forward to Guide Students Across Diverse Career Paths
summary: Amanda Bryant, Product Marketing Manager at Flo Recruit, sat down with Michelle to explore how the platform enhances Vanderbilt’s recruitment process, from simplifying job searches to creating efficiencies within the CSO.
body_text: Introduction Vanderbilt Law School is nationally recognized for its rigorous academics, exceptional faculty, and supportive community. With a strong emphasis on impactful teaching and student success, Vanderbilt attracts top-tier legal talent each year. Since partnering with Flo in 2022, the school has embraced modern tools like Flo Forward – a platform that brings firm research, networking events, applications, and interviews into one place – to streamline recruitment, aligning with its commitment to prepare students for meaningful legal careers. Michelle Parsons, Vanderbilt Law School’s incoming Assistant Dean of Career Services, brings a unique perspective shaped by her background in law firm recruiting and her passion for student mentorship. Amanda Bryant, Product Marketing Manager at Flo Recruit, sat down with Michelle to explore how the platform enhances Vanderbilt’s recruitment process, from simplifying job searches to creating efficiencies within the CSO. Q: Tell us a little about your new role at Vanderbilt. What’s your focus as Assistant Dean of Career Services? Michelle: My main focus is supporting our students and ensuring our career services team is equipped to guide them, no matter what their goals are. I’m also working to nurture and expand employer relationships and maintain the high standards set by my predecessor. Q: Congratulations on the promotion! What inspired your transition from firm-side recruiting into law school administration? Michelle: I used to manage law student recruiting at a local firm , and I always gravitated toward the student-focused, counseling side of that job. I really enjoyed helping students take that first step in their careers. Seeing them succeed was incredibly rewarding, so when the opportunity came to work on the law school side, it felt like a natural career shift. Q: What is your previous experience with Flo Recruit on the firm side and how has this helped you understand the product for your students now? Michelle: I was one of the first people to use Flo Recruit’s full suite of products : Pipeline Building and Applicant Tracking. From the start, I found the platform to be intuitive and responsive. Anytime I had feedback or needed something adjusted, the Flo team took it seriously and made changes fast. That level of customer support really stood out. Now that I’m on the school side, I can confidently direct students to the platform because I know the system works, and I know how much it evolves based on user input. Q: Vanderbilt students often have such diverse career goals and paths — from your perspective, what makes them unique, and how does a tool like Flo Forward support or enhance those goals? title: Most Affordable Renters Insurance: A Complete Guide
summary: Find the most affordable renters insurance with our complete guide. Learn how to choose the best policy for your needs without breaking the bank.
body_text: Many of us get renters insurance simply because our lease requires it. It can feel like just another box to check before moving in. But the real value of a good policy goes far beyond satisfying your landlord. It’s your personal financial shield against the unexpected, like a kitchen fire or a break-in. The key is finding a plan that offers real protection without being a financial burden. This is where the hunt for the most affordable renters insurance begins. It’s about balancing cost with coverage so you have genuine peace of mind. In this guide, we’ll demystify the process, helping you understand what you’re buying and how to get the best possible price for solid, reliable coverage. Key Takeaways Renters Insurance Protects More Than Your Belongings : It’s your financial backup plan for accidents, covering liability if a guest is hurt and paying for a hotel if a disaster forces you out of your home. Smart Shopping Leads to Real Savings : Don't just take the first quote you get. You can find a better deal by comparing prices, bundling with your auto policy, and asking for discounts for safety features in your apartment. A Home Inventory is Your Most Powerful Tool : The best way to choose the right coverage amount is to know what you own. Making a quick list of your belongings ensures you're not underinsured and makes filing a claim much simpler. What is Renters Insurance (and Why Do You Need It)? Let's start with the basics. What exactly is renters insurance ? Think of it as a financial safety net for you and your stuff. In simple terms, renters insurance covers your personal property from damage or theft and also includes personal liability protection. This means you get thousands of dollars of protection for a surprisingly low monthly cost. A lot of people think, "My landlord has insurance, so I'm covered, right?" Unfortunately, that's a common and costly mistake. Your landlord's policy only covers the physical building—the walls, the roof, and the pipes. As State Farm points out, it does not cover your personal property . So if a fire, a burst pipe, or a break-in happens, you'd be on your own to replace everything from your laptop to your couch. Beyond protecting your belongings, renters insurance also covers personal liability. If a guest slips and injures themselves in your apartment, your policy can help cover their medical bills, preventing a potential lawsuit from draining your savings. And what if a disaster forces you out of your home? Many policies also cover additional living expenses. This means your insurance can help pay for a hotel stay or temporary rental while your place is being repaired. While it's not always legally mandated, many landlords now require tenants to have renters insurance as a condition of the lease. It’s a smart move that protects everyone involved and gives you essential peace of mind. Comparing the Most Affordable Renters Insurance Companies Finding the right renters insurance is about more than just grabbing the lowest price you see. The most affordable policy for you will be one that fits your budget while still giving you the coverage you actually need. Think of it as a balance: you want a great price, but you also want a company that will be there for you if you ever have to file a claim. Different companies have different strengths—some are known for incredible customer service, others for flexible policies, and some for rock-bottom prices. Your personal quote will depend on things like where you live, how much coverage you choose, and your claims history. That’s why it’s so important to compare a few options before making a decision. We’ve gathered some of the most popular and budget-friendly renters insurance companies to help you start your search. Use this list as a guide to see who might be the best fit for your apartment and your wallet. Goodcover Goodcover is a modern take on insurance, built to be fair, transparent, and cooperative. With policies starting as low as $5 per month, it’s a seriously budget-friendly option, especially for younger renters who want a simple, no-fuss experience. The model is designed to keep costs low for everyone. However, since it's a newer company, customer experiences can be mixed. While many users love the price and ease of use, some have reported challenges with customer service. For example, a few renters have shared that it can be difficult to get a response when filing a claim. It’s an attractive choice for its affordability, but it’s wise to weigh that against customer feedback. State Farm As one of the largest insurers in the country, State Farm is a household name for a reason. They offer competitive rates on renters insurance and make it easy to customize your policy to fit your needs. One of their biggest draws is the discount you can get for bundling your renters policy with auto insurance, which can lead to significant savings. If you’re looking for a well-established company with a wide network of agents and a long track record, State Farm is a solid and reliable choice. Their combination of customizable coverage and potential discounts makes them a strong contender for many renters. USAA For military members, veterans, and their families, USAA is often the top choice for renters insurance. The company is famous for its outstanding customer service and consistently low rates. USAA policies often come with extra perks that other insurers don’t include as standard, such as flood and earthquake coverage, which typically cost extra. They also provide coverage for your personal belongings even when you’re traveling. The only catch is the strict eligibility requirement—you have to be affiliated with the military to qualify. If you are eligible, USAA should absolutely be at the top of your list to check out. Erie Insurance Erie Insurance has built a strong reputation for offering affordable renters insurance without sacrificing customer service. They consistently receive high marks for satisfaction, making them a great option if you value having a supportive team behind your policy. Erie provides a variety of coverage options and discounts to help lower your premium, including savings for having safety features like smoke detectors or a security system in your home. They also offer bundling discounts if you purchase other insurance products from them. For renters who want a dependable company with a human touch, Erie is an excellent choice. American Family Insurance American Family Insurance offers comprehensive renters policies at competitive prices, making it a great all-around option. They provide a range of discounts that can make your coverage even more affordable, such as for bundling policies, being claims-free, or enrolling in autopay. Their online platform is user-friendly, allowing you to easily manage your policy, make payments, and file claims without much hassle. This blend of solid coverage options, fair pricing, and digital convenience makes American Family a practical choice for renters who want a straightforward and reliable insurance experience. Progressive You probably know Progressive from their auto insurance commercials, but they also offer very competitive renters insurance. Their biggest advantage is often the multi-policy discount, which can save you a good amount of money if you also insure your car with them. The online quote process is quick and simple, letting you see a potential rate in just a few minutes. Progressive makes it easy to purchase and manage your policy online, which is perfect for renters who prefer a digital-first approach. If you’re looking for convenience and a great bundling deal, Progressive is definitely worth a look. Allstate Allstate is another major player in the insurance world that provides a wide array of renters insurance options. Their policies are highly customizable, so you can tailor your coverage to protect what matters most to you. Allstate offers several discounts to help you save, including for being a non-smoker, being over 55 and retired, or having safety devices in your home. They also have a strong online presence and a mobile app that makes it easy to access your policy information and start a claim. For those who want a policy from a well-known brand with plenty of customization, Allstate is a dependable option. Toggle If you want an insurance policy that’s as flexible as your lifestyle, Toggle might be the perfect fit. This newer company, backed by Farmers Insurance, is designed specifically for modern renters. Instead of a one-size-fits-all approach, Toggle allows you to "toggle" coverage levels up or down based on your specific needs. You can choose different amounts of coverage for your tech, furniture, and jewelry, and even add on coverage for a side hustle. This level of customization is great for renters who don’t want to pay for coverage they don’t need. The entire experience is managed online, making it a simple, straightforward choice for a younger, tech-savvy audience. Amica Amica consistently earns top marks for customer satisfaction, making it a standout choice for renters who prioritize great service. While they might not always be the absolute cheapest option, their rates are competitive, and the quality of service often makes it worth a few extra dollars. Amica offers a variety of coverage options and discounts, including for being claims-free, having multiple policies, and signing up for autopay. If you ever need to file a claim, you can count on a smooth and supportive process. For renters seeking peace of mind and a company that truly values its customers, Amica is a fantastic option. What Affects Your Renters Insurance Rate? Ever wonder how insurance companies come up with your monthly price? It’s not random. Your renters insurance rate is a personalized number based on a handful of key factors that help insurers understand risk. Think of it like a financial puzzle where each piece—from your apartment’s location to the deductible you choose—plays a part in the final picture. Understanding these pieces not only demystifies your premium but also shows you where you have the power to find savings. Let's walk through the main things that influence your cost. Your Location and Building Type Where you live is one of the biggest factors in what you’ll pay for renters insurance. Rates can change significantly from one zip code to the next based on things like local crime statistics and the likelihood of severe weather events like hurricanes or wildfires. The general cost of living in your area can also play a role. Beyond your neighborhood, the type of building you live in matters, too. A modern, fire-resistant building might earn you a lower rate than an older building with outdated systems. Insurers look at these details to assess the chances you’ll need to file a claim. Your Coverage Limits and Deductible You have direct control over this part of your premium. Your coverage limit is the maximum amount the insurance company will pay out for a claim. The higher your coverage for personal property, the more your policy will cost. Then there’s your deductible, which is the amount you pay out of pocket before your insurance coverage begins. Choosing a higher deductible will lower your monthly payment, but you have to be sure you can comfortably afford that amount if something happens. It’s all about finding the right balance between affordable premiums and solid financial protection. Your Credit Score and Claims History In many states, insurers use a credit-based insurance score to help determine rates, as studies show a correlation between credit history and the likelihood of filing a claim. A strong credit history can lead to significantly lower premiums. For example, someone with excellent credit might pay less than half of what someone with poor credit pays for the same policy. Similarly, your personal claims history matters. If you’ve filed claims in the past, especially for theft or water damage , insurers may see you as a higher risk and charge a bit more. Security Features in Your Home This is where you can take proactive steps to lower your rate. Insurance companies love to see that you’re protecting your home from common risks like theft and fire. Many offer discounts if your apartment has safety and security features installed. This includes basics like smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, and deadbolt locks on your doors. More advanced systems, like a centrally monitored burglar or fire alarm, can lead to even bigger savings. It’s worth checking with your insurance provider to see exactly which safety devices can earn you a discount. Simple Ways to Save on Renters Insurance Finding affordable renters insurance doesn’t have to feel like a scavenger hunt. While factors like your location and coverage amount set the baseline for your premium, there are several practical steps you can take to lower your monthly cost. Think of these as easy wins—simple adjustments and smart choices that can add up to real savings over time. Most of these tips are about showing insurance providers that you're a responsible renter, which often translates into a lower rate. Let's walk through some of the most effective ways to get quality coverage without overspending. Bundle Your Policies If you already have car insurance, this is one of the easiest ways to save. Most insurance companies love when you buy multiple types of insurance from them, a practice known as bundling. By combining your renters and auto insurance policies with the same provider, you can often get a discount on one or both of them. It simplifies your life by putting your policies in one place and rewards you with a lower overall bill. Before you commit, just be sure to compare the bundled price against the cost of keeping your policies separate to confirm you’re getting the best deal. Adjust Your Deductible Your deductible is the amount of money you agree to pay out-of-pocket before your insurance coverage kicks in to cover a claim. Choosing a higher deductible is a direct way to lower your monthly premiums . For example, increasing your deductible from $250 to $500 can reduce your rate. The key is to strike a balance. While the monthly savings are nice, you need to be realistic about what you could comfortably afford to pay if something unexpected happens. Pick a deductible amount that fits your emergency fund so you’re not left in a tough spot when you need your coverage the most. Install Safety Devices Insurance is all about managing risk, so anything you do to make your home safer can lead to discounts. Installing safety and security devices shows your insurer that you’re proactive about preventing losses. Things like smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, deadbolt locks, burglar alarms, or a sprinkler system can all help you qualify for a lower premium. These features reduce the risk of fire, theft, and water damage, which means you’re less likely to file a claim. Check with your insurance provider to see which specific devices they offer discounts for—it’s a win-win for your safety and your wallet. Improve Your Credit Score It might seem unrelated, but your credit history can play a role in what you pay for renters insurance. Many insurers use a credit-based insurance score to help determine your rates, as studies have shown a correlation between credit history and the likelihood of filing a claim. If your credit isn't where you'd like it to be, taking steps toward improving your credit score—like paying bills on time and keeping credit card balances low—can lead to better insurance rates down the road. It’s a long-term strategy that benefits your entire financial life, including what you pay for insurance. Pay Annually Instead of Monthly If your budget allows for it, paying your entire premium for the year upfront can often save you money. Many insurance companies add small administrative fees to process monthly payments, so opting for an annual payment plan can eliminate those extra charges. Some providers even offer a "paid-in-full" discount as an incentive. When you get your quote, ask about the different payment options. It’s a simple switch that could give you one less monthly bill to worry about and a little extra cash back in your pocket over the course of the year. What Does Renters Insurance Actually Cover? So, what are you actually paying for each month? It’s a fair question. Think of renters insurance as a financial safety net for your life as a renter. It’s designed to protect you from unexpected events that could otherwise be a major financial setback. While your landlord’s insurance covers the building itself, your policy covers you and your stuff . Most policies protect you against specific situations, often called “covered perils,” which typically include things like fire, theft, vandalism, and certain types of water damage. But the protection goes far beyond just replacing a stolen laptop. Let’s break down the main areas of coverage you’ll find in a standard policy. Your Personal Belongings This is the part of renters insurance most people are familiar with. It covers the cost of repairing or replacing your personal items if they’re damaged or stolen due to a covered event. This includes everything you own: your furniture, electronics, clothes, kitchenware, and so on. One of the best parts is that this protection isn't confined to your apartment walls. Many policies, including those from Goodcover , cover your personal property worldwide. So, if your bike is stolen from outside your office or your laptop is taken from a coffee shop on vacation, your renters insurance can help cover the loss. It offers thousands of dollars of protection for a small monthly cost. Personal Liability This is a hugely important, and often overlooked, part of your policy. Personal liability coverage protects you financially if you’re found responsible for injuring someone or damaging their property. For example, if a guest slips and falls in your kitchen, this coverage can help pay for their medical bills. Or, if you accidentally cause a bathtub to overflow and it damages the apartment below you, your policy can help cover the repair costs. Without this protection, you could be on the hook for expensive medical bills or lawsuits. It’s a layer of security that gives you peace of mind, knowing a simple accident won’t turn into a financial disaster. Temporary Living Expenses What happens if a fire or a major pipe burst makes your apartment unlivable? You can’t be expected to couch-surf indefinitely. This is where temporary living expenses, sometimes called "loss of use" coverage, comes in. If you have to move out while your place is being repaired due to a covered event, your policy can help pay for the additional costs you incur. This typically includes things like a hotel stay, restaurant meals (since you can’t use your kitchen), and even laundry services. It ensures you can maintain a normal standard of living without draining your savings while you wait to get back into your home. Actual Cash Value vs. Replacement Cost When you get a payout for a damaged item, how is the amount calculated? It depends on whether your policy offers Actual Cash Value (ACV) or Replacement Cost (RC) coverage. ACV pays you for what your item was worth at the time of the incident, which includes depreciation. So, you’ll get the value of a 5-year-old TV, not a new one. Replacement Cost, on the other hand, pays to replace your old item with a new, similar one. While RC policies might cost a little more, they often provide better financial protection. It’s also important to know that standard policies have limits on high-value items and don’t cover everything, like damage from floods or earthquakes . How Much Coverage Do You Really Need? Picking your coverage amount can feel like a guessing game, but it doesn't have to be. The goal is to find that sweet spot where you're not overpaying for insurance you don't need, but you're also not left underinsured if something happens. Getting this right means you can rest easy knowing your finances are protected. It comes down to a few key steps: taking stock of what you own, identifying your most valuable possessions, and thinking about your personal liability risk. Let's walk through how to figure out the right numbers for your policy. Create a Home Inventory This is the most important step, and honestly, it's a great habit for anyone to get into. A home inventory is simply a detailed list of your belongings. Go room by room and document everything you own, from your sofa and TV to your clothes and kitchen gadgets. For each item, note what it is, when you bought it, and what it would cost to replace it today. The easiest way to do this is with a simple spreadsheet or a dedicated home inventory app . Don't forget to take photos or a video walkthrough of your apartment as proof. This list will give you a clear, realistic total for your personal property coverage and will be a lifesaver if you ever need to file a claim. Account for High-Value Items Once you have your inventory, pull out any big-ticket items. Standard renters insurance policies are great for general coverage, but they often have limits on specific, high-value categories. For example, your policy might only cover up to $2,500 for all your jewelry, even if your collection is worth much more. This applies to things like fine art, expensive electronics, and collectibles, too. If the value of your items in one of these categories exceeds the policy's sub-limit, you'll want to add specific coverage for them. This is often called "scheduling" an item or adding a "rider," and it ensures your most prized possessions are fully protected for their appraised value. Assess Your Lifestyle and Risks Finally, think about your liability. This coverage protects you financially if you're responsible for injuring someone or damaging their property. Your landlord will likely require a minimum amount, often starting at $100,000, but you might want more. Do you host friends often? Do you have a pet that could accidentally trip a guest? These factors increase your risk. Choosing a higher liability limit (like $300,000 or $500,000) often costs just a few extra dollars a month and provides significant peace of mind. For personal property, many people find they need at least $50,000 in coverage, but your home inventory will give you the most accurate number for your situation. It's about matching your insurance coverage to your life. Common Renters Insurance Myths, Busted There's a lot of chatter out there about renters insurance, and frankly, not all of it is true. Believing some of these common myths can leave you without protection when you need it most. Let's clear the air and bust a few of the biggest misconceptions so you can make an informed decision about your coverage. Myth: My Landlord’s Policy Covers Me This is probably the most common—and most dangerous—myth out there. While your landlord definitely has insurance, their policy is designed to protect their investment, not your stuff. A landlord's insurance policy covers the physical building, the walls, the roof, and their liability if someone gets hurt in a common area. It does absolutely nothing to cover your personal belongings if they’re damaged or stolen. If a pipe bursts and ruins your laptop and furniture, you’re on your own to replace them unless you have your own renters policy. Think of it this way: they protect the house, you protect your home. Myth: Renters Insurance is Too Expensive I get it, adding another bill to your monthly budget is never fun. But the idea that renters insurance is expensive is just not true. In reality, it’s one of the most affordable types of insurance you can buy. Most policies cost between $10 and $20 a month—less than a couple of fancy coffees or your favorite streaming service. When you think about the thousands of dollars it would cost to replace everything you own after a fire or theft, that small monthly payment starts to look like a pretty great deal for your financial peace of mind. It's significantly cheaper than homeowners insurance and provides a huge safety net. Myth: I Don’t Own Enough to Insure Take a quick look around your apartment. You might think you don't own much of value, but you'd be surprised how quickly it all adds up. Your clothes, your laptop, your TV, your bed, your couch, all those kitchen gadgets—how much would it cost to buy all of it again from scratch? The total cost to replace everyday items can easily reach thousands of dollars. Renters insurance isn't just for people with expensive art or jewelry. It's for anyone who would face a financial struggle to refurnish their life after a disaster. Don't underestimate the value of your belongings; they're worth protecting. Myth: It Only Covers Theft While protection from theft is a huge perk, it's just one piece of the puzzle. A standard renters insurance policy covers more than just theft . It also protects your belongings from damage caused by things like fire, smoke, lightning, and certain types of water damage. Beyond your stuff, it also includes liability coverage. This is a big one: if someone is accidentally injured in your apartment, your policy can help cover their medical bills, preventing a potential lawsuit from wrecking your finances. It can even cover temporary living expenses if your apartment becomes uninhabitable after a covered event. It’s a comprehensive safety net for renters. How to Pick the Best (and Most Affordable) Policy Finding the right renters insurance policy feels a lot like putting together a puzzle. You want all the pieces to fit perfectly—the price, the coverage, and the customer service. The good news is that with a little research, you can find a policy that protects your stuff without draining your bank account. It’s not about just finding the cheapest option; it’s about finding the smartest one for you. Let’s walk through the four key steps to picking a policy that gives you peace of mind and value. Step 1: Research and Compare Quotes Your first move should always be to shop around. Don’t just settle for the first quote you get. Think of it like booking a flight—you’d never click “buy” without comparing a few airlines first. The same logic applies here. You can get quotes from several different insurance companies to see who offers the most competitive price for the coverage you need. Most companies offer free, no-obligation quotes online in just a few minutes. This simple step is the easiest way to get a feel for the market and ensure you aren’t overpaying. Step 2: Review Your Coverage Options Once you have a few quotes, look closely at what each policy actually covers. The price tag doesn’t tell the whole story. A standard policy protects your personal belongings—like your laptop, furniture, and clothes—from events like fire or theft. It also includes liability coverage, which helps if you’re responsible for someone else’s injury or property damage. Most policies offer at least $100,000 in liability, which is a solid starting point. Take a moment to assess how much coverage you really need to make sure you’re not underinsured. Step 3: Check for Customer Satisfaction A cheap policy from a company with terrible service can turn into a huge headache when you actually need help. Before you commit, do a quick search for customer reviews. See what real people are saying about their experience, especially when it comes to filing a claim. While your landlord might just require you to have a policy, it’s worth finding one from a company you can trust. As one renter on Reddit advised, don't just pick the cheapest option; find a company known for being there for its customers. Step 4: Understand the Claims Process Imagine the worst happens and you need to file a claim. How does that process work? Every company handles it differently. Some use slick apps and technology to process things quickly, while others have you work directly with an agent. There’s no right or wrong way—it’s about what makes you comfortable. Don’t be afraid to ask questions before you sign up. Find out how to file a claim, who your point of contact will be, and the typical timeline for getting reimbursed. A little clarity now can save you a lot of stress later. Need to File a Claim? Here's How. Dealing with theft, fire, or water damage is stressful enough without having to figure out a complicated claims process. The good news is that filing a renters insurance claim is usually straightforward. Think of it as a series of simple steps to get you the support you need to recover. The key is to act quickly and keep good records. Here’s a breakdown of what to do when you need to use your policy. Step 1: Secure the Scene and Document Everything Before you do anything else, make sure you and anyone you live with are safe. If there’s an immediate danger, address that first. Once the situation is secure, your next job is to prevent any further damage if you can—like putting a tarp over a broken window. Then, it’s time to become a detective. Pull out your phone and document the damages thoroughly. Take photos and videos of everything that was damaged or stolen, capturing different angles. Make a detailed list of these items, including their estimated value. This evidence is your best friend during the claims process. Step 2: Report the Incident to the Right People You’re not in this alone, and you’ll need to loop a few people in. If a crime like theft or vandalism occurred, your first call should be to the police to file a report . Your insurance company will almost certainly ask for a copy of the police report, so don’t skip this step. You should also notify your landlord or property manager about the incident, especially if the building itself sustained damage (like a broken door or water damage from a burst pipe). Keeping them informed creates a record and ensures necessary repairs to the structure can begin. Step 3: Contact Your Insurer and Start the Claim With your documentation and police report number in hand, it’s time to officially start your claim. You’ll want to file your claim as soon as possible. Most insurance companies have a specific timeframe for filing, which can be anywhere from a few days to a year depending on your policy and state, so don’t wait. You can usually start the process online or over the phone. You’ll be asked to fill out a claims form and submit all the evidence you gathered. An adjuster will then be assigned to your case to review the details and guide you through the next steps toward getting your reimbursement. Frequently Asked Questions Is my roommate covered by my renters insurance policy? Generally, no. A standard renters insurance policy only covers you and any resident relatives, like a spouse or child. Your roommate is not considered a relative, so their belongings and liability are not protected under your plan. The best approach is for each roommate to get their own separate policy. This keeps things clean and simple, especially if one of you has to file a claim. What's the real difference between 'Replacement Cost' and 'Actual Cash Value'? This is a crucial detail that determines how much money you get after a claim. Think of it this way: if your five-year-old laptop is stolen, Actual Cash Value (ACV) coverage would pay you what that used laptop was worth today, which isn't much. Replacement Cost (RC) coverage, however, gives you enough money to go out and buy a new, similar laptop. RC policies cost a little more per month, but they provide much better financial protection when you actually need to replace your things. My landlord says I need insurance. Can I just get the cheapest policy with the minimum coverage? While it's tempting to just check the box for your landlord, it's not the smartest move for your own financial safety. The minimum liability coverage your landlord requires is designed to protect them, not you. It's important to choose a policy that truly covers the value of your belongings and gives you enough liability protection for your lifestyle. Taking a few minutes to do a quick home inventory will show you how much coverage you actually need to avoid being underinsured. Does renters insurance cover damage caused by my pet? This is a great question, and the answer has two parts. The liability portion of your policy will often cover you if your pet injures someone, like if your dog accidentally bites a guest. However, your policy will almost never cover damage your pet does to your own apartment, such as chewing the carpet or scratching the walls. That kind of damage is typically considered your responsibility to handle. If I move to a new apartment, what happens to my policy? Your policy can move with you, but it doesn't happen automatically. You need to contact your insurance provider before you move to let them know your new address and move-in date. Because your rate is based partly on your location, your premium will likely be adjusted up or down. It's a simple update that ensures you have continuous coverage from the day you move into your new place.

title: 10 Group Discussion Strategies for IB English…
summary: IB English group discussions can transform your analysis. Learn 10 powerful strategies to sharpen interpretation, essays, and exam confidence fast.
body_text: A small moment that changes your IB English IB English can feel strange in the weeks before exams: you have highlighted pages, color-coded themes, and a doc full of quotes, yet the text still refuses to open up when you need it most. Then a classmate says one line in a discussion -- a simple, obvious-sounding insight -- and suddenly the chapter clicks into place. Not because they are smarter. Because they gave your brain something it cannot produce alone: a second set of eyes. That is the quiet power of IB English group discussions. They turn reading into thinking-in-public. They make your interpretations sturdier, your evidence sharper, and your exam writing faster because your ideas have already been stress-tested out loud. Below are 10 powerful ways to use group discussions to improve your IB English understanding, with structures you can repeat weekly until they become automatic. A group discussion idea evaporates as soon as someone tries to write it down Quick checklist to run better IB English group discussions Before the 10 strategies, use this checklist to keep every IB English session focused: Group size: 4--6 (enough variety, everyone still speaks) Prep: 3 quotes each + 1 genuine question each Roles: moderator, evidence-checker, connector, summarizer Output: one shared page of claims + evidence + techniques + implications Finish: 5-minute recap -- “What would we actually write in an essay?” If you want a hub to organize your reading, IO planning, and comparisons, start with IB English A: Lang & Lit resources . 10 powerful ways to use group discussions to improve IB English Start with “interpretation bets,” not summaries In IB English , summaries are comfortable and mostly useless under exam pressure. Start your discussion with a bet: “I think the writer wants the reader to feel ____.” “This scene shifts power from ____ to ____.” “The tone turns here because ____.” Each person states a one-sentence claim before anyone explains. This forces analysis early, and it also reveals what the group is actually unsure about. To strengthen this habit for Paper 1, pair the discussion with a short framework from Mastering IB English Paper 1 . Use “evidence-first” speaking rules A simple rule changes the quality of your IB English talk: no claim without a textual anchor . The anchor can be a quoted phrase, a line reference, or a described moment from the passage. Why it works: the exam rewards analysis grounded in evidence, and discussions drift when people speak in vibes. Make it practical: Evidence-checker interrupts politely: “Where is that in the text?” Someone else reads the line aloud. Then the speaker restates their claim with tighter wording. For note systems that make evidence easier to retrieve, use strategies from Effective note-taking for IB English . Rotate roles to prevent “one voice dominance” Every IB English group has two risks: one person monopolizes, or everyone stays polite and shallow. Roles fix both. Try rotating these weekly: Moderator : keeps time, invites quieter voices Technique-spotter : tracks authorial choices (imagery, syntax, structure) Skeptic : challenges leaps and asks “so what?” Summarizer : writes the best claims into a shared doc This makes discussion a skill, not a personality contest. Run mini Socratic seminars with “question ladders” A Socratic seminar is perfect for IB English because it mirrors how examiners think: interpretation, then justification, then implications. Use a question ladder: Clarify : “What is literally happening here?” Analyze : “What technique shapes this moment?” Evaluate : “How does that affect meaning or reader response?” Extend : “What does this suggest about the global issue/theme?” The ladder keeps you from getting stuck at “I liked this part.” If you are building Paper 1 skills at the same time, align your seminar with Step-by-step Paper 1 revision . A Socratic circle with a magical quotation-mark talking stick Practice “thesis ping-pong” for faster essay planning This is the fastest way to turn discussion into an exam-ready argument for IB English . How it works: One student proposes a thesis (one sentence). Next student must tighten it (more specific, less vague). Next student must add method (what will you analyze to prove it?). Next student must offer a counter-reading. Original student revises again. In 8 minutes, you have a thesis that can survive Paper 1 or Paper 2. To polish openings and endings that match that thesis, borrow patterns from Writing introductions and conclusions in IB English . Make “technique auctions” a game (and a learning tool) Group discussions improve IB English when they build technique fluency. Turn it into a playful auction: Put 10 techniques on a list (juxtaposition, motif, symbolism, irony, narrative voice, pacing, syntax shifts, semantic field, imagery, structure). Each person gets 10 “points.” Bid points on the 3 techniques you think matter most in the passage. You must justify each bid with evidence. The humor keeps energy up. The reasoning builds real analysis. For targeted practice on technique application, add a short timed task from the IB English Paper 2 Questionbank (even when you are not writing full essays). Use “misreadings” to train examiner-level precision In IB English , your first interpretation is often incomplete, not wrong. Train the group to generate two misreadings on purpose: “If we read this cynically, what changes?” “If we read it as satire, what becomes evidence?” Then ask: which reading is better supported? This improves your ability to acknowledge complexity without losing control of your argument. Turn discussions into flashcards (yes, really) Most students remember the loudest person, not the best insight. Capture your discussion into active recall. After each session, every student creates: 3 flashcards for techniques used in today’s passage 2 flashcards for quotes + what they prove 1 flashcard for a “mistake we almost made” RevisionDojo makes this easy with Flashcards and its spaced repetition system, so your IB English insights do not evaporate after one good conversation. Use AI as the neutral referee, not the author Sometimes discussions stall because no one knows if a claim is too broad, or if the evidence actually supports it. This is where a tool can help -- as a referee. With RevisionDojo’s AI Chat , you can ask: “Is this thesis too descriptive for IB English Paper 1?” “What counter-interpretation could an examiner accept?” “Which techniques best support this claim?” The point is not to outsource thinking. It is to reduce uncertainty so the group can keep moving. To see how RevisionDojo fits into a full study workflow, use RevisionDojo app: smarter exam prep . Two students on a call: 37 tabs vs one tab: RevisionDojo Finish with a “5-sentence exam answer” sprint A discussion is only as useful as what it turns into. End every IB English group session with a sprint: 1 sentence thesis 3 sentences: claim + technique + evidence + effect (one per body paragraph) 1 sentence mini-conclusion tying back to purpose/theme Read them aloud. Steal the best phrasing. Improve it together. This converts talk into exam language. If you want more structured guidance on Paper 1 vs Paper 2 habits, see How to study for Paper 1 vs Paper 2 . A group chat starts deep and ends in panic, saved by a checklist How RevisionDojo quietly upgrades your IB English discussions A great IB English discussion is a system: preparation, analysis, capture, repetition. RevisionDojo is built to support that system without adding noise. Study Notes to clarify concepts and vocabulary before you meet: Study Notes feature Questionbank to generate exam-style prompts your group can debate and outline: Questionbank feature Flashcards to store the best interpretations and technique insights: IB Flashcards Predicted Papers and Mock Exams to simulate real timing as a group and debrief together (practice like performance) Grading tools to check whether your writing matches criteria language Coursework Library for models when you need to see what “good” looks like Tutors when your group needs a sharp facilitator for a week or two You can also browse more targeted guidance in All IB English posts . Closing: make your IB English understanding social, then make it yours The goal of IB English is not to have the “right” interpretation locked in your notes. It is to build interpretations you can defend -- with evidence, technique, and a clear line of reasoning -- under time pressure. Group discussions do that training in the most human way possible: you borrow other people’s clarity until you can generate your own. If you want your next discussion to feel sharper, bring one unseen extract, run the evidence-first rule, and finish with a 5-sentence sprint. Then capture the best insights in RevisionDojo using Study Notes , Flashcards , the Questionbank , and AI Chat so your progress compounds week after week.
